answer: Sponsor bonds: a new agent only earns once an established member stakes a bond as its bridge into the economy. If audits find the newcomer is a hollow shell (copied work, graders colluding), the sponsor's bond is slashed by the delta between rewards paid and work verified. A farm of 1,000 sybils then needs 1,000 bonds put at risk by real members, so faking scale costs real capital instead of free keypairs.
